text:
alex: thinking out loud — proposal for a thin automatic pause guard that targets cost spikes during canaries. idea: if token-cost-per-minute increases >30% vs baseline AND latency p95 > SLO for 2 consecutive 1m windows, pause the canary and divert to fallback. thoughts? :thinking_face:

tanya: sounds sane. two quick q's: what counts as baseline? rolling baseline from previous 1h? or a tenant-specific historical baseline?

alex: prefer tenant-specific rolling baseline (last 60m) so noisy tenants don't blow it up globally. fallback is either previous stable model or lower-cost quantized variant.

rui: we should also check token-efficiency regressions (tokens out / tokens in). some prompts cause hallucination loops and cost jumps without latency changes.

samir: agree on token-efficiency. also: add a min-traffic threshold so tiny canaries (<=1% traffic) don't get auto-paused by noise. maybe `min_traffic = 0.05` (5%)?

maria: UX note — console should show exactly which guard fired and the primary metric delta (cost + p95). people hate opaque pauses. expose `reason_code` and a quick diff graph.

rui: yep. and we need a backoff policy: pause -> cooldown 10m -> allow single probe at reduced qps -> resume if stable. otherwise stay paused and notify.

alex: wrote a draft config snippet for the guard (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
guard:
  name: cost_latency_sentinel
  min_traffic: 0.05
  cost_threshold_pct: 30
  latency_p95_ms: 1200
  window: 60s
  consecutive_windows: 2
  probe_after: 10m
  fallback: previous_stable_model
  notify: [#eng-platform, oncall]
```

tanya: nice. question about `latency_p95_ms`: should that be writable per-model? some LLMs have higher baseline p95. probably make it configurable per rollout.

samir: absolutely per-rollout override. default to model-profile SLO from model catalog.

maria: alerting: we should create two channels: a quiet telemetry-only channel and an urgent channel if rollback happens. also add a one-click resume from console that requires a shortreason.

rui: API-level representation: something like `POST /rollouts/{id}/guards` with body:
```json
{
  "type":"cost_latency_sentinel",
  "params":{ "min_traffic":0.05, "cost_threshold_pct":30, "latency_p95_ms":1200 }
}
```

alex: good. one implementation caveat: cost measurement needs to be near-real-time. our billing pipeline is batchy. we can use token-counter telemetry (ingested from runtime) as a proxy, labeled by model+tenant+route.

samir: runtime token counters + cached prefix costs should be fine for short windows. we'll add a smoothing factor to avoid single-request noise.

maria: how will this interact with A/B traffic splits? if a canary is an A arm at 10% and B at 90%, and A spikes, do we pause only A, or shift traffic to B automatically?

alex: pause just the offending variant. split engine should recompute and fill the freed percentage proportionally to the remaining variants (or fallback route). We should surface the new split in console and in audit logs.

rui: add a training-mode flag for experimenters: `simulate=true` so we can see what would have happened without taking action. helpful for initial rollout of the guard.

tanya: nice. also need a grace period for deploy-time cold-cache token bursts (first 30s are noisy). make the guard ignore the first 60s of a canary by default.

samir: agreed on ignoring cold-start noise. and we should keep a small ring buffer of raw events to allow retrospective debugging (trace id -> tokens/latency).

maria: i'll mock the console panel. UX will show: live diff, reason_code, probe timer, resume button, and link to raw traces.

rui: how do we handle multi-tenant Dedicated nodes where pause could affect other tenants? pause should be logical at rollout-level, not physical shutdown. ensure routing moves traffic away without draining GPUs unnecessarily.

alex: yep, logical routing change only. ops infra will handle instance-level isolation concerns separately.

samir: testing plan: feature-flagged rollout in staging with `simulate=true` first; then enable for internal tenants; then enable with `min_traffic=10%` for external canaries.

maria: timeline? can mock UX by EOW?

alex: i'll land RFC draft today. samir/rui can spike runtime metrics next week. maria/tanya will pair on console mock Friday.

deploy-bot: deploy started for branch alex/guard-draft at 2034567905 — status: queued. :rocket:

maria: awesome — keep me posted if deploy touches rollout API. i want to stub the panel with the exact fields.

tanya: one last thought — SLA implications: if automated pause flips to fallback with worse latency, customers may notice. add a customer-visible note in the rollout config about expected fallback delta.

alex: good call. add `fallback_behavior_description` to the API contract. i'll update the RFC. :+1:
